Light Transmittance Marching is a technique to compute physically accurate lighting in a volume by casting a secondary raymarch from each sample point on the primary view ray towards the light source to calculate absorbed light (transmittance) [S1, S2, unofficial].

Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describe a technique where, for each sample point on the primary view ray, a secondary raymarch (or nested loop) is performed towards the light source. This secondary march samples the density along the path to calculate the accumulated density, which is then used (via Beer's Law or an exponential function) to compute the transmittance (or transmissance) of light absorbed by the volume. This matches the claim's description of computing physically accurate lighting by calculating absorbed light via a secondary raymarch.
